proof_attempt_summary: Attempted the full primitive-confounding cubic benchmark-dose risk and honest-length frontier. Derived admissible normalized-confounding lower alternatives and an observable derivative-informed honest upper, but the resulting bracket leaves a 1/7 versus 2/23 root-exponent gap at s_mu=s_pi=1,d=10 and an unresolved observational logarithm; the original matched rate outputs remain open. Corrected the doubled value allowance and public threshold, verified citations, and obtained a clean D0.5 math review; the incremental partial result was banked below the field floor without entering Lean formalization.
tldr: For an unknown cubic crossing of a monotone causal risk curve, the proved result is a same-class risk-and-length bracket with computable data-only decisions. The lower root scale is \(\max\{n^{-1/7},n^{-2(3l+v)/(3d+7(l+v))}\}\), where \(l=\min(s_\mu,s_\pi)\) and \(v=\max(s_\mu,s_\pi)\); the upper root scale is the existing \(\nu_n\). The squared-risk scales are their squares. The cell-root interval is connected and uniformly honest at level \(0.9\) at every finite sample size, with its public full-\(B\) fallback. The polynomial exponents agree at \(1/7\) when \(d\le3T_*\), with \(T_*\) defined in the cell upper rate, but the observational logarithm remains unresolved. Beyond that regime the exact polynomial rate and critical logarithms remain unresolved. The randomized submodel retains exact logarithm-free risk and length rates \(n^{-2/7}\) and \(n^{-1/7}\).
gap: Existing causal-dose theory supplies conditional correction bounds or flatness limits with negligible nuisance remainders. It does not determine all-procedure precision for a displaced cubic contact under primitive confounding restrictions.
fill: Derivative-sensitive localized corrections and shape-preserving normalized mixtures address the two sides of one risk-and-length frontier. Public bias allowances and localized test inversion address finite-sample coverage without presuming a canonical flatness law.
